Pipeline arguments from a malariasimulation site file

Source: R/site.R
site_to_pipeline.Rd

Turns one unit of an Imperial malariasimulation site file (e.g. a foresite calibrated, scaled site, reduced to one unit with site::subset_site()) into the arguments for pipeline, so magenta runs on the site's calibrated EIR without its own fitting.

site_to_pipeline(
  site,
  years = NULL,
  burnin = 20,
  burnin_interventions = c("none", "first"),
  drug_list = drug_list_create(),
  irs_scale = 0.75,
  net_type = "pyrethroid_only",
  update_length = 365
)

Arguments

site

Site file for one unit, e.g. from site::subset_site()

years

Calendar years to run after the burn-in. Default = all years with treatment coverage in the site file

burnin

Years of burn-in before years. Default = 20

burnin_interventions

"none" (default) or "first", see Details

drug_list

Drug list used for ft, see site_ft

irs_scale

Multiplier on the site's IRS coverage. Default = 0.75

net_type

Net type in site::net_efficacy. Default = "pyrethroid_only"

update_length

Days between updates in pipeline, which must divide 365. Default = 365

Value

Named list of arguments for pipeline, with attributes year (calendar year of each simulated year, burn-in included) and tx_cov (the site's treatment coverage in each simulated year, e.g. for severe_outcomes)

Details

  • EIR: the site's pf EIR (adult EIR, as magenta's EIR).

  • Seasonality: site_seasonality.

  • Burn-in: burnin years before the first site year. With burnin_interventions = "none" the burn-in has no treatment, ITNs or IRS (so the starting equilibrium is at ft = 0); with "first" it holds the first year's values.

  • Yearly interventions: itn_cov is the site's ITN use, irs_cov the site's IRS coverage times irs_scale (0.75, the adjustment malariasimulation runs apply), and ft from site_ft with drug_list. Years missing from the site are 0.

  • Nets: d_ITN0, r_ITN0 and r_ITN1 are dn0, rn0 and rnm from site::net_efficacy (net_type) at the unit's pyrethroid resistance, averaged over the site years weighted by ITN use (magenta has one net efficacy for the whole run). The ITN half-life is gamman * log(2) (malariasimulation's decay is exp(-t / gamman)), and nets are aged with the "constant" clock over a life of the site's retention half-life (see itn_decay_clock in model_param_list_create). This is the mean efficacy of nets in use when nets are topped up every year to hold use steady, as the site's yearly distributions do. Without a retention half-life the net life is 3 years.

  • Vectors: Q0, bites_Bed, bites_Indoors and mu0 are the species means (weighted by prop) of Q0, phi_bednets, phi_indoors and mum.

  • Demography is not set: magenta's population is exponential with a mean age of 21 years in the individual model, whatever eta, so the site's demography is not used.

Drugs, resistance, non-malarial fevers, barcodes and the other pipeline arguments are left to the user: add them to the returned list. Use the same drug_list here and in pipeline.

The aim is to put magenta in the right transmission setting for scenario modelling of drug resistance, not to reproduce every intervention in the site file. Only treatment, ITNs and IRS are used: SMC, PMC, vaccines and larval source management in the site file are not modelled, and IRS uses magenta's default efficacy whatever the insecticide.

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
s <- readRDS("calibrated_scaled_site.rds")
unit <- site::subset_site(s, data.frame(name_1 = "Busia", urban_rural = "urban"))
args <- site_to_pipeline(unit)
out <- do.call(pipeline, c(args, list(N = 10000)))
} # }
